text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions describe exactly what they do. For example, a function called "calculateTotal" is much better than one called "calc" or "x". You should also keep functions small and focused on a single task. This makes your code simpler to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time. When you return to a project months later, readable code saves you hours of confusion.
